Write a caller result to a directory

Source: R/call_scn.R
write_scphasedcn.Rd

Flat tables: cells.tsv (cell, qc, stratum, fold, null_cell, n_calls, n_events, clone / posterior / doublet_like / ref_pool when present), calls.tsv (cell- and clone-level calls: called rows in normal mode, all inherited / confirmed rows in tumour mode), pooled_calls.tsv (called pool rows), events.tsv, thresholds.tsv, null_fit.tsv (depth t rows + rho), false_calls.tsv + false_events.tsv (normal mode), tumour mode: clones.tsv, assignments.tsv, clone_segments.tsv, clone_profiles.tsv.gz, reference_pool.txt; regions.tsv; result.rds (the object without scores and features), params.yaml, summary.tsv (scphasedcn_summary()) and NOTES.md. Optional: scores.tsv.gz, features.tsv.gz. The files of a previous result in out (the names above) are removed first, so a re-run never leaves stale tables behind (e.g. clones.tsv of a tumour run, scores.tsv.gz of a run with write_scores); other files in out are left alone. An object without scores (or features), e.g. one read back with read_scphasedcn(), leaves an existing scores.tsv.gz (features.tsv.gz) in place: it cannot write them again.

Usage

write_scphasedcn(obj, out, write_scores = FALSE, write_features = FALSE)

Arguments

obj

scphasedcn from call_scn()

out

output directory (created)

write_scores

also write the per cell x region scores

write_features

also write the features long table

Value

named character vector of the written paths, invisibly
